strengths: Identifies and quantifies an important practical problem: foundation FM priors significantly underperform domain-specific and untrained priors for solving IPs, with clear experimental evidence (Table 1, Figs. 2-3)
Theoretically motivated approach using concentration-of-measure results to explain why existing initialization fails and justify the time-dependent warm-start strategy
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (DIV2K, AFHQ, RealSR), tasks (4 linear IPs), metrics (6 metrics), and thorough ablation studies demonstrating necessity of components
Strong empirical results: FMPlug achieves consistent improvements over D-Flow baseline and approaches domain-specific FM performance, particularly valuable for scientific IPs with few samples
Novel extension to few-shot setting for scientific IPs addresses real practical constraints (cost of data collection and model training) in scientific imaging domains
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, complete results, and robustness analysis (Table 17 shows remarkably low variance)
Well-motivated problem identification and clear presentation of motivation, intuition, and empirical validation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: warm-start is straightforward (learnable time parameter), shell constraints for Gaussianity are from Yang et al. 2024; primary contribution is combination rather than fundamental new techniques

Theoretical gaps: connection between CoM (Theorem 3.1) and practical performance is intuitive but not rigorously established; surjectivity claim (Table 2) based on limited empirical evidence (1000 images); no convergence analysis for non-convex joint optimization in Eq. 3.7

Few-shot setting assumptions violated in practice: for MRI, spatial concentration of instances causes large performance gap (23.60 vs 28.71 PSNR for Red-Diff); assumption that instances are close to unknown x may not hold universally
Severe computational cost: FMPlug ~50-70× slower than interleaving methods (492s vs 7-10s, Table 9), limiting practical applicability despite superior quality; no analysis of quality-speed tradeoffs
Inconsistent performance on no-reference metrics: CLIPIQA/MUSIQ often underperform (sometimes by 0.1-0.3), and dismissing these metrics as unreliable feels defensive when they are widely used

Limited experimental scope: only image-based IPs tested; single foundation model backbone (Stable Diffusion V3); scientific IPs limited to 3 tasks from InverseBench; generalization to videos, 3D, other modalities unclear

Incomplete hyperparameter guidance: ε=0.025 based on limited sensitivity analysis (3 values); learning rates appear dataset-dependent without principled generalization strategy; no guidance for new problems

Comparison fairness concerns: methods use vastly different NFEs (3 vs 6 vs 28); 'strengthened' baselines (FD-S) show minimal improvement in Table 1, raising questions about implementation or genuine ineffectiveness
